context.objective: Understand the current process, responsibilities, handoffs, and exceptions.

turns.text: The payment preparer starts when there is an approved obligation and proposed payment instructions. They enter the payee, amount, purpose, entity, value date and folder reference in the Payments Log where those fields exist. They set the status and check whether instructions are new or changed. Either condition requires a callback.
During the callback, what does the preparer verify about the payment instructions?

The callback performer uses an approved independent source for the phone number, never the instruction email. They call the known contact, verify the name and relationship, compare payee and account-holder names, and verify IBAN and SWIFT in Europe or ABA in the US plus other applicable account details. They record who called, contact, relationship, date and time, keeping only permitted masked bank details.
What happens if the callback details do not match the payment instructions?

Stop if the contact cannot be reached, details conflict, or payee and account-holder names do not match. The procedure leaves the escalation owner and threshold unspecified. We cannot release on that basis. On a verified payment, the reviewer still matches the invoice and checks duplicates, Exiger sanctions/high-risk-country screening and UK CIS where applicable. A potential high-risk-country match goes to two Signatory A approvers.
After the reviewer’s invoice, duplicate, screening, and CIS checks, what permits the payment to be released?

For a US payment, client approval is required before release. European payments follow the applicable FA-18 regulated approval sequence and a capital-adequacy check where applicable. Treasury checks cash against pending payments, cutoff and value date, retains a balance screenshot and arranges FX as needed. If funds are short the status becomes Insufficient Funds and FA-16 takes over. Otherwise the preparer inputs the payment at the bank for Signatory 1 and an independent Signatory 2 to approve, plus two Signatory A approvals when required, before schedule or release.
What confirms that a payment has been executed?

Treasury monitors the final bank status and updates the Payments Log from In Progress to Settled, Pending Query or Not Paid by GPFS as applicable. Returns, rejects and queries are investigated, and changed instructions are verified again before resubmission. The preparer files the approval, callback, screening, balance, payment and final bank-status records in the binder or payment folder, links it in the log, and obtains AFC-or-higher sign-off that the records are complete.
Once Treasury marks a payment Settled, what—if anything—happens next to close it out?
